correctness.rationale: After A starts in a part X, B choosing X forces all future play inside X and terminal length n_X; B choosing a different part forces at most one vertex per part and terminal length k. Thus A wins achievement iff k is odd and some n_i is odd, and wins avoidance iff k is even and some n_i is even. Combining these criteria gives the four-case correction and the order-six minimal examples.
correctness.risk: The conclusion is specific to complete multipartite graphs with all parts at least two.

final_claim: For \(K_{n_1,\ldots,n_k}\) with \(k\ge2\) and all \(n_i\ge2\), B wins both general-position achievement and avoidance exactly when either k is odd and all parts are even, or k is even and all parts are odd; otherwise the games have opposite winners, and the smallest counterexamples to the published claimed equivalence are exactly \(K_{3,3}\) and \(K_{2,2,2}\).
limitations: The component source propositions are not challenged.
